title: THE HERO ON YOUR LOBBY SCREEN IS THE HERO IN YOUR MATCH
hook: A painted soldier that never changes is a lie the player catches on day two. Ours is the same 36,000-triangle GLB that takes the field.
facts: The lobby hero is hero.glb rendered live in a WebGL stage over a photographed empty bay — one asset, two contexts.
GPU is rented only while visible: play on entry, pause on exit, dispose before the engine boots.
Keyart went from a 2.8 MB PNG to a ~430 KB JPEG q90 without a visible seam in the audit frame.
take: One asset, two contexts — the lobby IS the match renderer. Everything else is marketing.
question: What is the one asset in your project that never gets a stand-in?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the empty deploy bay photograph, and the live rig standing on it.

title: FOUR THEATRES, ONE 116 MB PROMISE
hook: Most web games hide their download behind a spinner. Ours prints 116,282,422 bytes on the door and refuses to open until the debt is paid.
facts: Four theatres — Frostline Relay, Verdant Bloom, Emberfall Foundry, Vanguard Station — open from one committed WASM + PCK payload.
The boot screen prints the exact byte debt before it opens: 116,282,422 bytes, no spinner lies.
PCK 76,767,668 B across 873 files; WASM 39,514,754 B — both measured in CI, both printed at boot.
take: Honest boot beats fast boot: the door prints the debt before it opens.
question: What does your loading screen promise — and what does it actually measure?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the four-theatre world plate, and the boss vantage from the world tour.

title: NINE HUE FAMILIES, ONE AUDITABLE PALETTE
hook: Concept art that adds a tenth colour family is not 'more interesting'. In our build, it is a bug that fails the pipeline.
facts: Nine hue families, contract-enforced: any texture above 8% off-palette fails the build.
9/9 families ship clean; drift measured per texture, not per screenshot.
The palette contract lives in CI, so art direction is a test result, not an opinion.
take: A palette is a contract. Ours fails the build at 8% drift.
question: How does your team enforce art direction — reviews or tests?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the dashboard plate at 0.2% off-palette, and the loading keyart poster.

title: PLAYTEST PASS 07 — THE BROWSER PLAYED BACK
hook: We let a headless browser play our own game for 30 seconds. The rifle reloaded. That is the whole headline.
facts: Scripted input for 30 s — walk, aim, fire, reload — pulse rifle logged 23/24 then a clean G-reload in the HUD.
Weapon voice shot_pulse_rifle fired through the real audio pipeline; 14 sounds synthesised in 208 ms on boot.
The EMP chip read READY the entire pass and the mute toggle reached the audio pipeline mid-fight.
take: If a headless browser can play it for 30 seconds, a human probably can too. Probably — which stays UNVERIFIED.
question: What is the shortest playtest you would trust?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the aim pose mid-pass, and the walk cycle that opened it.

title: WORLD REVIEW CAMERA — EIGHT DISTRICTS, ONE PASS
hook: Eight keys, eight districts, one camera pass. The world finally fits in a single screenshot set.
facts: The review camera frames all eight districts without a cut — four theatres plus staging, on one continuous world.
Every district frame holds the nine-family palette: 0.2% max drift against the audited colour contract.
Blockout massing now reads from altitude: rooftops, rails and relay masts silhouette before textures do.
take: A world you cannot frame in one camera pass is a world you cannot review.
question: How do you review a world before it has textures?
visualNote: Two district frames travel with this post, straight from the review camera.

title: THE ENCOUNTER GATE STAYS HONEST
hook: Our own playtest refuses to start the defense until a human says ready. So do our claims.
facts: Explore stays a safe zone by design: no hostiles until START DEFENSE is pressed — the log prints it every session.
Defense remains UNVERIFIED in headless runs: software WebGL is slow, and we will not claim a mode we have not timed.
The gate is the promise: built and tested gets claimed, everything else gets listed as unverified in the same font.
take: The gate is the product promise: nothing claimed before a human says ready.
question: What does your game refuse to claim about itself?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the safe-zone pad, and the gate structure from the review camera.

title: HUD THAT READS AT A GLANCE, 720P
hook: Vitals, objective, weapon state: three blocks, one glance, zero tutorial.
facts: The 720p HUD keeps vitals, the objective card and the weapon block in fixed corners — readable in a single eye sweep.
A HUD MOBILE toggle exists in the build, but touch play on a physical device is still listed UNVERIFIED.
Active weapon reads PULSE RIFLE 23/24 with reload and armory hints on one line — no menu diving mid-fight.
take: HUD is UI copy: three blocks, one glance, zero tutorial.
question: What does your HUD say when the player is losing?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the third-person HUD at 720p, and the dashboard plate.

title: AUDIO SYNTH, NOT SAMPLES: 208 MS
hook: Fourteen sounds, synthesised in 208 milliseconds, zero sample files shipped. The mix is code.
facts: The whole session audio kit — 14 voices — is synthesised at boot in 208 ms; the PCK ships no sample library.
First voice landed 10.6 s after synthesis in the headless pass: pipeline latency is measured, not assumed.
Mute and unmute reach the live pipeline mid-session without restarting a single voice.
take: Synth audio is a payload decision: 14 voices, 0 sample bytes.
question: What does your audio pipeline cost in bytes?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the aim pose the weapon voice fired under, and district 3 at rest.

title: WEBGL2 IS THE FLOOR, NOT THE CEILING
hook: WebGPU is at 85.72% of global traffic. WebGL2 is at 96.44%. We ship to the floor and profile the ceiling.
facts: caniuse pull 2026-10-09: WebGPU full support 85.72% (+3.05% partial), up from 28.53% in Jan 2024.
WebGL2 sits at 96.44% and WebAssembly 96.63% — why nearly every 2026 production web game still ships a WebGL2 path.
Godot's web export stays WebGL2-only through 4.8-beta1; Unity 6.6 moved WebGPU out of experimental but keeps it off by default.
take: Render on the floor, profile the ceiling weekly. The migration date is a number, not a vibe.
question: What is your WebGPU fallback threshold — and what measures it?
visualNote: Two plates travel with this post: the renderer-floor audit, and our dashboard at 0.2% drift.

title: SOFTWARE WEBGL PROVES RENDERING, NOT PHONES
hook: Our headless playtest runs on software WebGL2. It proves the build renders. It proves nothing about your pocket.
facts: Every capture in this feed comes from headless Chromium with SwiftShader: real engine, real input, zero GPU.
Which is exactly why every mobile claim in our posts carries UNVERIFIED until device data exists.
1280x720 canvas, HUD readable, rifle reloaded — rendering evidence, labelled as rendering evidence.
take: A test you cannot run on target hardware is still evidence — of something narrower. Say which.
question: How do you label the gap between CI evidence and device truth?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the aim pose the headless pass captured, and the walk cycle before it.

title: GODOT 4.8-BETA1: NEW TOYS UPSTREAM, SAME FLOOR DOWNSTREAM
hook: Godot 4.8-beta1 landed 15 Oct with Trail3D, multi-bounce AO and contact shadows. Our web build did not move an inch — and that is the point.
facts: 4.8-beta1 (15 Oct 2026): native Trail3D, multi-bounce AO approximation, screen-space contact shadows, dockable main screens.
Web export docs still read WebGL 2.0 only — no WebGPU path for Forward+/Mobile on web.
We run 4.7.2-stable in the web preview: 39.5 MB wasm, 34 MB pck, 2/2 browser QA green.
take: Engine upgrades are cheap; renderer migrations are not. We migrate on browser-share numbers, not release notes.
question: How do you decide when a renderer floor is safe to leave?
visualNote: Attached: a 16:9 capture of the source article — read it there, our stance is here.

title: THE DECOMPILED-PORT WAVE HAS A PROVENANCE PROBLEM
hook: Halo, Vice City, Cyberpunk — decompiled into browser tabs by models overnight. Some nuked by DMCA in hours. None shipped a receipt.
facts: Oct 2026 wave: AI-decompiled ports of Halo CE, GTA Vice City and Cyberpunk 2077 running in browsers via Wasm + WebGPU.
The GTA V port went live and was taken down within hours; Xbox opened a lab for AI-created ports on 13 Oct.
WebGPU approaching 90% global support is why these ports run at all — the same floor we audit weekly.
take: A port without provenance is a demo. A release without evidence is a promise. We publish the difference.
question: Where should the line sit for AI-decompiled ports of shipped games?
visualNote: Attached: a 16:9 capture of the source article — read it there, our stance is here.

title: ENGINE-SWAP SEASON: LOYALTY IS A COST LINE
hook: RimWorld left Unity for an in-house engine and got 2-4x. Turing Complete left Godot after a years-long rewrite. GameMaker goes free-commercial in 2027.
facts: RimWorld 1.7 (12 Oct 2026): Unity to in-house Waylith engine, same look, 2-4x performance in studio tests.
Turing Complete 2.0 swapped Godot for a custom engine and compiler — a rewrite that took years.
GameMaker's GMRT runtime goes free for commercial use in Jan 2027.
take: We stay on our engine for audited reasons — web export, payload size, test count — and we re-run that audit every quarter. Loyalty with receipts.
question: What would make you swap engines mid-project — and what evidence would you require?
visualNote: Attached: a 16:9 capture of the source article — read it there, our stance is here.

title: FAILURE POSTS OUTPERFORM SUCCESS 3-5X. WE PUBLISH BOTH ANYWAY.
hook: The data says confessing beats celebrating by 3-5x. That is exactly why the ledger cannot be a growth hack.
facts: Build-in-public measurements put failure posts 3-5x above milestone posts.
The trap: audiences of supporters cheer confessions and never buy — overlap between readers and buyers is the real metric.
Our ledger line ships in the same font as the wins, on good weeks and bad ones.
take: If honesty is scheduled for engagement, it is advertising. Ours is scheduled because the wins need a witness.
question: Would you still publish the unverified list if it measurably hurt reach?
visualNote: Two plates travel with this post: the ledger, and the frame it audits.

title: EVIDENCE, NOT NOISE: THE TO-DO LIST IS NOT CONTENT
hook: 'Shipped dark mode' is a to-do list wearing a megaphone. Build-in-public dies exactly there.
facts: The field's failure mode: daily updates nobody outside the team can use — broadcasting, not building in public.
The working mode: decisions with reasons, screenshots with numbers, failures with dates.
House rule: every post carries a number, a frame, or a confession. Zero of three means it does not post.
take: Content is the audit trail of decisions. Everything else is status.
question: What is your filter for 'worth posting' — and what did it kill this week?
visualNote: One plate travels with this post: signal over noise, in the house palette.

title: FIRST LIGHT: THE WAVE NOW BRIEFS YOU BEFORE IT TESTS YOU
hook: Chapter 01 opened in our headless pass this morning: FIRST LIGHT, objective survive the wave, one CONTINUE between us and the arena.
facts: The encounter now opens on a briefing card — chapter, objective, one button — no auto-start, no ambiguity about what is about to be tested.
Behind it the deployment shell lists operative, theatre and arsenal with real stats — DMG 18, rate 5/s, mag 24, reload 1.35 s — before a single shot exists.
Defense itself still reads NOT OBSERVED under software WebGL in headless — the prep frames are evidence of the gate, not of the wave.
take: A wave you can refuse to start is a wave you can measure twice.
question: What does your game show in the three seconds before the first fight?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the FIRST LIGHT briefing card, and the deployment shell behind it.

title: THE ARENA MOVED ITS MASTS OFF THE SPAWN RING
hook: Cover is the east module now. The relay masts that used to crowd the spawn ring are gone, and the lane breathes.
facts: Oct 24 world pass: relay masts moved off the spawn ring, turrets flanked, centrepiece box skipped — the arena lane stays open at 6 m per side.
The monument is measured from the origin where the forge puts it, not from where a human remembered it last week.
Every one of those moves landed with a forge-verify import report in the same batch: 3 worlds checked, 0 failed, 259 animation clips counted.
take: Level design with a tape measure in the commit message is level design that survives review.
question: What is the one layout rule your team refuses to break?
visualNote: Two frames travel with this post: the arena after the mast move, and the walk lane that proves it open.

title: NO TEXTURE SYNTHESIS: FOUR SURFACES, GRADED NOT SCANNED
hook: There is no texture synthesis anywhere in our pipeline. Four real surface families, graded into the palette by code that admits what it did.
facts: Kit surfaces are graded, not scanned: gradeKit() re-maps authored material colours; gradeNature() lerps nature tones into the nine-family contract.
The one scanned plate in the set was lifted legally and graded on top — the licence cleanup sits in the same commit as the grade.
The night pass keeps it honest: emissive veins and lamp pools hold the audited palette under a ringed-planet skybox.
take: Procedural-looking does not mean procedural. Ours is authored, graded, and receipted.
question: Where does your art pipeline draw the line between authored and generated?
visualNote: Two world renders travel with this post: Frostline's defence line and Verdant's overview, straight from the world docs.

title: THREE WORLDS, FIFTEEN RENDERS, ONE SELECTOR THAT NEVER WORKED
hook: The world selector shipped broken: the launcher never used the short ids. One human clicking through all three worlds found it in a minute.
facts: Confession first: letting a world id select itself fixed a launcher that ignored short ids — the bug shipped because nobody clicked past world one.
The same batch documents all three worlds with their own in-engine renders: five frames each for Frostline, Verdant and Emberfall.
Those renders now do two jobs: review evidence in the world docs, and the media attached to this post.
take: Renders are not marketing. They are the review meeting that scales.
question: What does your team review with images instead of meetings?
visualNote: Two world renders travel with this post: Verdant's overview and Emberfall's yard under the smelter lights.

title: DEV TRANSMISSION W44 — THE RECEIPT CUT
hook: Twenty-four seconds, eight shots, one promise: nothing in this video is announced — every frame is a receipt.
facts: The receipt cut: crane rise over the FIRST LIGHT gate, crash zoom into the arena lane, whip pan to Frostline, speed ramp into the defense gate.
Three odometers settle on the week's numbers — 116,282,422 boot bytes, 259 forge-verified clips, 9 hue families under contract.
It closes on the ledger in amber: the unverified list, same font, same weight as the wins.
take: A product video that ends on its own unverified list is a product video people trust.
question: Would your promo dare to close on what it has not proven yet?
